agent: deploy menu drop onto the order of battle browser, 2026-11-13
question: Can a deploy menu line be dragged onto a row of the order of battle browser, and what does the drop do? (FINDINGS-deploymenu.md section 6 had it only as inferred, and placed the drag on the map.)

structs.name: CDeploymentMenuMouseObserver
structs.comment: The deploy menu's mouse observer (base CSideMenuMouseObserver), polled each frame by CSideMenuDeploy::Update through its slot 1. **It does not watch the map**: it hands a deployment line held down by the player to the order of battle browser as a drag, once the pointer is inside the browser's window. Made inline by CSideMenuDeploy::CSideMenuDeploy (operator new 0x1C) and owned by the menu (CSideMenu +0x28). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md, section 6.
structs.evidence: operator new(0x1C) and the field stores at 0x8277C1-0x8277F5 (+4 = [0x174DAA8]+0xE4, +8 = the menu, +0xC = the constructor's second argument, +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 = 0), vftable 0x15E02E4 written at 0x8277E9 (VA; rva 0x11E02E4) and confirmed by RTTI (CDeploymentMenuMouseObserver, 2 slots). Would be wrong if the RTTI export put the table elsewhere.

structs.name: CDropAndAssignUnitDeploymentCallback
structs.comment: What the browser calls with the row's unit when a deployment line is dropped on a row: posts the CDeployUnitCommand. One slot (Call). Made only by CDeploymentMenuMouseObserver::OnMouse and owned by the observer (+0x14), which frees the previous one each time it starts a drag and in its destructor. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md, section 6.
structs.evidence: operator new(0xC) at 0x828D0F, stores at 0x828D34-0x828D3D (+0 vftable 0x15E02DC, +4 the deployment from 0x8274D0, +8 the observer's +0xC); the vftable is referenced exactly once in .text (findRefs --address 0x15e02dc: 0x828D39). RTTI gives the class 1 slot, base CUnitDeploymentCallback.

structs.name: CDeploymentEntry
structs.comment: A line of the deploy menu's plain list (window `deployment_entry`), base CStandardlistboxItem. Its `select` button has two handlers: the click (glue's first, through the slot-4 thunk 0x67A310: CDeploymentEntry::OnSelect, run when the left button is let go over the pressed button) and the press (glue's third: CDeploymentEntry::OnDragStart, run when the left button goes down on it). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md, sections 3 and 6.
structs.evidence: The constructor 0x826F40: the CRef built at +0x78 from the deployment argument (0x82703A, the reference builder 0x7C9530), +0xA0 = the in-game screen and +0xA4 = the menu (0x82704B, 0x827059); the glue at +0x28 built by 0x828E10 with 0x67A310 first and 0x827600 third (0x826FF5-0x827029).

structs.name: CUnitDeployment

addresses.name: CDeploymentMenuMouseObserver::OnMouse
addresses.comment: **Slot 1, polled every frame by CSideMenuDeploy::Update: hands a pressed deployment line to the order of battle browser as a drag.** It does not watch the map. Where the menu is not shown (its slot 4) or the browser (the in-game screen's slot 105, COOBBrowser) is not open (+0xF4), it clears pressed_entry and press_pending and stops. Where press_pending is 1 and the pointer (input slot 19) lies inside the browser's main window (+0xD0: its +0x18 slot 15 for the corner, its slot 24 for the size; both edges inclusive), it takes the unit the pressed line's deployment holds (CDeploymentEntry_GetUnit; none, nothing), frees its previous callback, makes a CDropAndAssignUnitDeploymentCallback (deployment, in-game screen), and starts the browser's drag with it: **the unit's only brigade by COOBBrowser::BeginDragSubUnit where the unit has exactly one (+0x40 == 1), else the unit by COOBBrowser::BeginDragUnit**; then clears pressed_entry and press_pending. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole, 0x828C20-0x828D80 (two bare `ret`s, the body bounded by 15 int3 at 0x828D81 and the next function at 0x828D90). The rectangle compared at 0x828CB3-0x828CE5 is built from [[menu+0x20] slot 105]+0xD0, i.e. COOBBrowser's window (record: COOBBrowser +0xD0 window), not from anything of the map; the old comment's 'map's rectangle' and 'left click' are refuted (no button test at all in the body). 0x8274A0 resolves the observer's +0x10 (the CDeploymentEntry, written by 0x827600) and returns its deployment's +0x38. Would be wrong if slot 105 of CInGameIdler were not the browser - FINDINGS-oobbrowser.md section 2 has it so.

addresses.name: CDropAndAssignUnitDeploymentCallback::Call
addresses.comment: Slot 0: posts CDeployUnitCommand(province = the unit's current province's id (+0x130, then +0xD0), country = the in-game screen's GetPlayer (slot 23), deployment = the id of the one held (+4), target = the unit) through the in-game screen's channel (slot 18, +0x38, slot 6). **Called by UnitRows_HandleDrop with the row's unit when a deployment line is dropped on a row of the order of battle browser** - not by anything on the map. It checks nothing itself. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole 0x826130-0x8261F4 (`ret 4`). Its only callers are indirect calls through the vftable 0x15E02DC slot 0 in UnitRows_HandleDrop (0x73A8D9 unit path, 0x73AB1D sub-unit path); the vftable is written only at 0x828D37 in OnMouse, which hands the object to BeginDragUnit/BeginDragSubUnit. The old comment's 'dropped on a unit on the map' has no code behind it.

addresses.name: UnitRows_HandleDrop
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall UnitRows_HandleDrop(void* drag, void* rows, CUnit* unit, CSubUnit* subUnit, CLeader* leader, int x, int y)
addresses.comment: **A unit, a brigade or a leader dropped on a list of the order of battle browser** (drag = the COOBBrowser; rows = its list or split list) - also the second way a CTransferSubUnitCommand is posted from the interface (0x33AB6C). `ret 0x1C`. Walks the rows (the list's +0x148); for each row whose element (+0x20) holds (x, y) strictly inside, by the element's slots 26 and 24, and whose unit (the reference at +0x28) is not the thing dropped's own: a **unit** - CUnit_MayTakeSubordinate(row's unit, unit, 0); allowed, **a deployment callback the browser holds (+0x98) is called with the row's unit (posting the CDeployUnitCommand) and cleared, and then a CAttachUnitCommand(unit, row's unit) is posted all the same**, and +0xF8/+0x120 keep the row's and the dropped unit's references; **no province test on this path**; a **sub-unit** whose unit is not the row's - CUnit_CanTakeSubUnit(row's unit, the country of the row unit's owner, subUnit, sameProvince = no deployment callback pending); refused, the callback is cleared and nothing is posted; allowed with a callback, the callback's deployment is asked CUnitDeployment::CanDeployIn(the row unit's current province, +0x130) - false, the callback is cleared and nothing is posted; true, the callback is called with the row's unit and cleared, and then CTransferSubUnitCommand(row's unit, subUnit) is posted; allowed with none, the transfer alone; a **leader** - CUnit::MayTakeLeader(row's unit, leader) and, where the row's unit has a real leader (slot 8), MayTakeLeader(the dropped leader's unit, +0x40, that leader); then CAssignLeaderCommand(row's unit, leader, 0) and, in the second case, CAssignLeaderCommand(the dropped leader's unit, the row's old leader, 0) - a swap. Answers true where the point was over a row, posted or not. Called twice by COOBBrowser::Update on release at drag state 3 (0x339F67 the main list, 0x339F89 the split list where the main answered false). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section B, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole 0x73A7C0-0x73AE70 (one `ret 0x1C` exit). Unit path 0x73A882-0x73AA1B: MayTakeSubordinate at 0x73A8BA, the callback's slot 0 at 0x73A8D9 with the row's unit, then CAttachUnitCommand::CAttachUnitCommand at 0x73A906 and the post through g_CCurrentGameState+0xBE8 slot 18 / +0x38 slot 6 at 0x73A9BE, unconditionally after the callback. Sub-unit path 0x73AA20-0x73AC28: sameProvince = sete([drag+0x98]==0) at 0x73AAB8; slot 10 of [callback+4] with [rowUnit+0x130] at 0x73AAF6 (CUnitDeployment slot 10 = CanDeployIn in the record's slot table); the callback at 0x73AB1D; CTransferSubUnitCommand at 0x73AB6C. The callers were read in COOBBrowser::Update: both run only after the drag state reached 3 and the button (input slot 12) reads released. This revises only the comment's account of the deployment paths and the callers, and raises the confidence, which rested on a partial reading.

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md, sections 2 and 6.

addresses.name: CDeploymentEntry::OnDragStart
addresses.comment: **The `select` button's press handler** (the glue's third, the place COOBUnitEntry::OnDragStart has in its row; GuiButton_HandleMouse reaches it through observer slot 4 when the left button goes down on the button). Where the line's deployment (+0x78) is a unit deployment (slot 8 answers 0x4B4) holding a unit (+0x38): the menu's observer gets pressed_entry = this line and press_pending = 1; otherwise both 0. Nothing else: no drag yet, no selection, no custom-game gate (COOBUnitEntry::OnDragStart has one). A building deployment's line cannot be dragged. Bare `ret`. The name is ours, after the browser row's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole 0x827600-0x82764A. Its only reference is the push at 0x827006 in CDeploymentEntry::CDeploymentEntry, third handler of the glue built by 0x828E10 - the slot COOBUnitEntry's constructor gives COOBUnitEntry::OnDragStart (0x735EB4) while giving the click handler first (0x735EBD), as this one gives the slot-4 thunk 0x67A310 (OnSelect) first. The event that reaches it: GuiButton_HandleMouse (0x6CFBE0) calls 0x6CFEE0 (every observer's slot 4) at 0xACFC4D on event sub-kind 3 with button 1 - the left button down - and the deployment entry's glue table 0x15E0408 has slot 4 = 0x6B6BC0, which jumps to the handler at glue +0x10, the third constructor argument.

addresses.name: GuiButton_PollMouse
addresses.comment: Slot 67 of the ordinary button (GuiObject_guiButtonType): a button's observers told from the input's state rather than from an event (GuiButton_HandleMouse, slot 1, is the event path). The state is +0x64; 3 (disabled) does nothing but slot 69. On a button not shown (+0x2C clear): every observer's slot 5, state 0. Shown: the left button (input slot 12) up with state 1 - state 2 and every observer's slot 2 (GuiButton_NotifyClick); down - state 1 and every observer's slot 4 (GuiButton_NotifyPress), on every call it stays down; with none of input slots 12, 13 and 11 down, state 2. Then slot 69 (GuiButton_ShowState) with the input. `ret 4`. **Who calls slot 67, and how often, was not read.** The name is ours: the class has no RTTI name.
addresses.evidence: Inferred. Decoded whole 0x6CFB00-0x6CFBD8 (two `ret 4`); slot 67 of the table at VA 0x1607698 (rva 0x1207698), in no RTTI table (vtable.py --holding). +0x2C as 'shown' follows GuiButton_HandleMouse's record; input slot 12 as the left button follows COOBBrowser::Update. Its callers were not searched, so whether it runs for a list row's button at all is open - nothing in the deploy-menu reading depends on it.

addresses.name: GuiButton_NotifyClick
addresses.comment: Calls slot 2 of every CButtonObserver on a button's list (EAX = the button's +0x48, the head at its +4, the next node at +8): **the click** - GuiButton_HandleMouse calls it when the left button comes up over a button in state 1 (pressed), first of the click's notifications (then 0x6CFEC0, the global hook, 0x6CFF00, slot 68), and on a keyboard shortcut; GuiButton_PollMouse too. A glue maps slot 2 to its first handler. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md, section 6.

addresses.name: GuiButton_NotifyPress
addresses.comment: Calls slot 4 of every CButtonObserver on a button's list (EAX = the button's +0x48, the head at its +4, the next node at +8): **the press** - GuiButton_HandleMouse calls it when the left button goes down on a shown button that takes the mouse, and sets the state to 1. A glue maps slot 4 to its third handler, which is where the order of battle browser's rows and the deploy menu's lines start a drag (COOBUnitEntry::OnDragStart, CDeploymentEntry::OnDragStart). addresses.name: GuiButton_HandleMouse
addresses.signature: void __fastcall GuiButton_HandleMouse(void* button@ECX, void* event@stack:4, int unused@stack:8)
addresses.comment: **The button widget's mouse handler**, slot 1 of the four button tables; `ret 8`. Read as far as its gates: a button whose state (+0x64) is 3 - disabled, slot 47's - takes the separate path at 0xACFD72; otherwise, for an event of kind 0 (event +8) on a shown button (+0x2C), **nothing at all where byte +0x84 is nought** (slot 38, GuiButton_SetTakesMouse); then event +0x10 == 3 with +0x14 == 1 (the left button down) sets state 1 and **tells every observer's slot 4 (GuiButton_NotifyPress) - the press, a glue's third handler, where the order of battle browser's rows and the deploy menu's lines start a drag**; 4 (up) over a held button state 2 and the press is run (GuiButton_NotifyClick - observer slot 2, a glue's first handler - then 0xACFEC0, the global hook at rva 0x1685878, 0xACFF00, slot 68); 5 sets state 0 (0xACFF20, 0xACFF40); the right button's down and up at +0x70 (0xACFF60 on the up); kind 1 (a shortcut, by its +0x74/+0x78 key pair against the event's) the same +0x84 gate, then 0xACFEA0 and 0xACFEC0. Event +0x18 = 1 marks it handled. The event's layout is inferred from these uses; the second argument is not read in what was read.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole 0xACFBE0-0xACFDA5 (VA; one `ret 8`). Adds only what the left-button-down branch calls - 0xACFEE0 at 0xACFC4D, whose loop calls [vft+0x10], observer slot 4 - and the helpers on the other branches; the rest of the comment is the existing reading, unchanged, and the confidence stays inferred because the event layout is still read only from its uses.

notes: 0x6CFEC0 (observer slot 1, with the button) and 0x6CFF00 (observer slot 5) are the click's other two notifiers, not named. 0x427520 is a CDeploymentEntry routine that enables or disables `select` by the custom-game flag (0x4208B0), with no direct reference in .text; not followed. The double command on a deployment drop (CDeployUnitCommand then CAttachUnitCommand or CTransferSubUnitCommand) is recorded on UnitRows_HandleDrop; what the second command does once the first has run was not traced.
